absent: Locked poll registration, removal, and interrupt helpers beyond the wrapper delegation shown.
Grace period and exclusion guarantees for network synchronization waits.
Namespace object lifecycle, reference counting, and migration rules.
Driver receive headroom operation contract and automatic sizing algorithm.
Header operation creation, parsing, and validation contracts and error handling.
Segmentation, aggregated receive, and completion callback contracts and packet ownership.
Aggregation hash computation and transmit selection behavior.
Notifier delivery order, veto rules, and extended acknowledgement handling.
Transmit lower layer status codes and completion predicate definition.
Per processor allocation failure handling and device managed release timing.

findings.text: Transmit queue access exposes lookup of a queue object by numeric position within the device queue array, plus a convenience that derives the position from the packet queue mapping field, and a direct reader for that mapping field.
A transmit iteration helper visits every configured transmit queue in ascending position order and invokes a caller supplied routine with the device, the current queue, and an opaque argument.

Sideband channel reporting clamps a negated traffic class count at zero. Forward headroom reporting returns zero for phony headroom devices and otherwise the needed headroom value. Receive headroom update delegates to an optional driver operation while reset requests automatic sizing with a negative sentinel. Machine layer private data is guarded by a type tag with typed get and set.

Machine layer private lookup succeeds only when the stored tag equals the requested tag and otherwise yields absence. The setter warns when replacing a set tag with a different tag and when data exists while the tag indicates none, then stores both values unconditionally.

Network namespace association offers plain, read copy update, and assignment forms operating on the device namespace holder. Private area conversion recovers the device object from its embedded private storage. Parent device and device type assignment helpers bind the generic device linkage.

Device serialization uses a per device mutex with symmetric acquire and release helpers. Interrupt assignment, weighted poll registration, configuration based registration, and poll removal acquire the mutex around their locked counterparts, so the locked variants require the caller to already hold it.

Poll handling registration provides weighted, default weight, transmit oriented, configuration indexed, and locked forms, plus locked and unlocked removal and interrupt association. Default weight forms forward to weighted forms with a shared default.

Transmit oriented registration marks the poll state as ineligible for busy polling before delegating. Configuration indexed registration records the numeric slot and binds the corresponding configuration entry from the device array before delegating. Removal pairs combine list detachment with a network grace period wait in both locked and unlocked paths.

Packet tap description carries protocol discrimination, outgoing filtering control, optional device restriction with wildcard meaning, tracker state, packet and batch delivery callbacks, socket matching predicate, packet socket domain context, private context, and list linkage for global membership.

Segmentation and receive aggregation support is modeled as a callback bundle for segment splitting, aggregated reception, and completion, plus a registry entry pairing protocol discrimination with priority, the callback bundle, and list linkage.

Per processor software counters exist in three widths: a four counter transmit receive packet byte form, an extended form adding receive and transmit loss counters, and a compact packet byte form. Each form embeds a tear free sequencer and requests alignment proportional to its counter count.

Counter update helpers advance receive and transmit packet and byte totals and loss totals on the current processor record under sequenced protection that starts before mutation and ends after. Variants cover single packet receive, multi packet transmit, compact totals, and individual or bulk loss accounting.

Per processor statistic allocation provides raw, kernel allocation, and device managed forms that reserve per processor storage and initialize the tear free sequencer on every possible processor before returning the area.

Link aggregation upper information pairs a transmit selection policy with a hash policy. Transmit policies cover unknown, random, broadcast, round robin, active backup, and hash based choice. Hash policies cover absence, layer two, layer three four combinations, extended hashes, source media with virtual LAN, and unknown. Lower state carries link readiness and transmit enable as single bit flags.
Default poll weight is 64.
Device event enumeration starts its first member at one and offload extended statistic type for layer three is one.

Device notification vocabulary distinguishes bring up and tear down phases with pre and going down precursors, registration lifecycle, capability and address and name and type changes, upper and lower topology linkage, tunnel and virtual LAN filter propagation, transmit queue length change, extended statistic control and reporting, and packet data path feature change.

Notification envelopes all begin with a common base holding the affected device and optional extended acknowledgement. Specializations add maximum transmission unit payload, changed flag mask, upper device with master and linking roles plus opaque upper data, lower state pointer, pre change address pointer, and offload reporting pointers selected by report kind.
Notification envelope helpers initialize the base with a device and empty acknowledgement, and provide read only access to the stored device and acknowledgement from a constant envelope.

Device enumeration over a namespace offers forward, reverse, read copy update, safe against removal, continuing from a cursor, bond membership filtered, indexed dump, and single step next plus first element forms, all anchored on the namespace device list or index table.

Plain iteration requires exclusion against list mutation while read copy update forms target lock free readers and safe forms allow removal of the current element. Continuing forms resume after a cursor. Bond filtering further restricts to slaves whose master matches. Indexed dump walks the by index table upward from a start key. Next and first helpers return absence at list ends or on empty membership.

Transmit submission provides plain queuing with no accelerator, accelerated queuing with a sideband device, and direct queuing to an explicit queue identifier. Direct submission releases the packet when completion is not reported and returns the lower layer status in all cases.

Packet release covers an unspecified reason form that forwards to a reason carrying form with a socket independent drop path. Device unregistration covers single device queuing without a batch list, namespace scoped queuing into a batch, and a batch completion form that performs no action in these fragments.

Link header handling provides construction with type and addresses and length, address extraction, protocol discrimination, length validation, and presence testing, each consulting optional device header operations and falling back to neutral zero or false when absent.

Length validation accepts frames at or above the hard header length, rejects frames below the minimum header length, delegates intermediate lengths to an optional validation operation when present, and otherwise rejects.
Non uniform memory drop accounting uses two separately cache aligned atomic counters. Reading sums both halves, adding attributes to one half selected by node parity, and reset clears both halves.

Node identification offers two build dependent definitions, one reading the current processor node value directly and one mapping the current processor identifier through a per processor node table, plus a helper mapping any processor identifier to its node.

Queue lookup warns once on position beyond the configured count yet still computes the addressed slot, so callers must not rely on the warning for safety. Machine layer lookup returns absence on tag mismatch rather than failing. Direct transmit ownership transfers to the callee on incomplete status via packet release.

Header helpers silently produce neutral results when operations are missing, which callers must distinguish from genuine protocol zero. The many device unregister batch helper is an empty operation in these fragments, so no teardown can be assumed from it.

Namespace read copy update access, read copy update device iteration and stepping, and sequenced counter updates require their respective read side or update side protection; plain namespace and list stepping require stronger exclusion or stable membership.
